An orange leg sliver is pulled away from the blue leg. Some small back holes reduce, but the seat/junction defect is worse. The complete chair silhouette survives.

The teacher orange back is mostly continuous with small holes. TR introduces a long conspicuous white vertical slit and additional narrow holes; the seat still has thin gaps and a rough lip. The complete chair body is retained.

START, FM and teacher retain a coherent box chair. TR has pronounced front/side/support breakup, spikes, holes and compressed body. Known small foot bar remains, with green E that does not certify the free body.
Cap retains the chair but creates a perforated jagged back crown and top holes against the more filled teacher back. Large under-arm side panels persist; no whole-body collapse.
Cap has more open/slivered back and a raised seat-side protrusion than teacher. Main chair remains recognizable.
Chair body remains similar, but cap produces narrow separated orange slivers beside the known leg and a larger local mismatch than teacher.
Cap has a more ragged perforated crown and irregular thin back strips than teacher; the full chair and seat survive, but the back is locally less coherent.
Teacher has a much more continuous lower back and relatively clean seat. Cap retains a shattered crown and a large missing/open lower-back region; the seat and legs remain recognizable.
Cap has more and longer white cuts in the free back panel than teacher, plus openings at the lower-back/seat transition; overall seat and legs remain recognizable.
